Organized significance assigned to information within a representational, relational, pragmatic, or system-relative context.
Meaning defined by how information changes the system own predictions, valuation, memory, action possibilities, or self-model.
A transformation from represented input to a meaning-bearing or action-relevant organization under declared rules.
The degree to which information bears on a current question, goal, prediction, value, or state transition.
Information characterized by its consequences for action, control, or goal-relative state change.
Information extractable by an external observer or classifier without establishing that it changes the system own transition structure.
Information whose intervention changes the transition structure of the system or its internal variables under matched context.

operationalization: Intervene on X under matched context and test whether transition structure of Y or the wider system changes.

A constraint imposed by available information on admissible states, inferences, predictions, or actions.
A change in represented state produced by newly available evidence or relation.
A reduction of recoverable distinctions under a declared mapping, channel, projection, or transformation.
A systematic difference between represented/transmitted structure and a declared reference structure.
A mapping to a shorter or lower-dimensional representation, potentially preserving selected task-relevant information.
A declared pathway through which signals or information can be transmitted or transformed.
Information bearing on the relative support for a claim under a declared inferential framework.
A proposition or structured assertion assigned an epistemic status and provenance.
A content that can be evaluated for truth or support independently of the specific sentence used to express it.
A represented distribution or commitment over propositions, hypotheses, or possible states.
A graded estimate of reliability, probability, or commitment associated with a representation, report, or inference.
The availability of multiple non-equivalent interpretations not yet resolved by context or evidence.
A declared discrepancy measure between meanings or concept representations; it is not automatically identical to PhaseNav angular distance.
A rule by which meanings of parts and their relations contribute to the meaning of a larger expression.
An invalid or explicitly gated operation in which salience, affect, frequency, or resonance is allowed to increase epistemic authority without evidence.
A coordinate defined modulo a period, so endpoint values differing by a whole period are identified.
Phase difference after quotienting out any common global phase contribution.
A common phase shift applied to all components; in a projective state it is an unobservable gauge direction.
Non-uniqueness of representation under transformations that leave declared observables unchanged.
Selection of one representative from each gauge-equivalence class for computation or comparison.
An integer counting oriented turns around a periodic coordinate or loop under specified topological conditions.
An equivalence class of nonzero vectors under multiplication by a nonzero scalar, or by global phase in the normalized complex case.
A map from a source state space into a projective space that preserves declared relations or observables.
The exact map |psi(V)>=d^(-1/2) sum_j exp(i phi_j)|j> with d=36, under which the PhaseNav complex overlap equals the Hilbert-space overlap.
The squared overlap magnitude between normalized projective states; in the 36-mode embedding it equals PhaseNav relational coherence.
The pure-state parameter-space metric tensor defined from derivatives of normalized state vectors; its physical metrological meaning requires a valid physical realization.
For the equal-amplitude 36-mode embedding, F_ij=4(delta_ij/d-1/d^2), with rank 35 and one global-phase null direction.
A metric on parameter space induced by mapping parameters into a state space carrying another metric.
A parameter-space direction that changes observable state geometry under the declared measurement model.
A parameter-space direction with zero local distinguishability under the declared metric or observation model.
One minus projective fidelity, locally approximated by one quarter of the QFIM quadratic form for small displacements.
A quantity computed from an ordered trajectory rather than only from its endpoints.
Gamma_PN=sum_k A_k, the ordered sum of PhaseNav edge connections along a trajectory.
The argument of the product of normalized overlaps around a closed sequence of projective states.
A relative phase defined from inner products of nonorthogonal states; closed products generate gauge-invariant geometric phase information.
A closed-loop quantity unchanged by local representational gauge transformations under the declared model.
A measure of nontrivial geometric transport or deviation from local flatness in a declared connection/metric structure.
A locally extremal or shortest path under a declared metric and domain.
